eventMetadata.context_description: Showers and thunderstorms tied to a broad trough of low pressure over the South China Sea suppressed Hong Kong’s daytime maximum on August 1, 2026, anchoring trader consensus at 28°C. Official Hong Kong Observatory forecasts projected a 24–28°C range under persistent cloud cover and heavy rain at times, consistent with observational data that prevented the stronger solar heating typical of August’s climatological average near 31–32°C. This alignment of forecast models and real-time conditions produced the overwhelming 99.9% market-implied probability for exactly 28°C. A realistic challenge would require revised official measurements showing a different peak—such as localized clearing that allowed brief warming above the expected envelope or post-event data corrections by the Observatory—but current guidance and historical analogs for similar trough-driven days make such shifts unlikely.
